notes: FROZEN (daemon=incapable, driver=gap:interrupt, route=frozen) — no phases, per the SKILL frozen rule. The CORRECT spec, asserted here and never weakened to the daemon limit: a discovered hermes session running in a scriptable terminal backend reports controllable once the backchannel toggle is on and the 'control' consent is granted; daemon-injected text drives ready -> working on that same session and the turn settles working -> ready; an interrupt cancels an in-flight turn and settles back to ready (never sticking in working); input is refused when the toggle is off, consent is missing, or no scriptable backend exists; the relay path is gated identically. Irrlicht cannot do ANY of that for hermes today, and for two different reasons. (1) PRODUCT: core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/agent.go leaves Control zero-valued AND declares no agent.ControlPermission(), so InputService.resolve's consent step (Granted("hermes","control")) can never pass — PermissionService.Start grants only DECLARED permissions even under IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all, Answer() rejects an undeclared pair with ErrUnknownPermission, and Snapshot() never offers the grant — hence controllable:false on every hermes row (handlers.go annotateControllable) and ErrControlDisabled on every SendInput/SendCommand/Interrupt, locally and via the relay. The terminal-backend half is already fine and adapter-agnostic (PIDManager.captureLauncher + Controller.Controllable = resolveBackend(Launcher) != backendNone), so this blocker is a ~6-line adapter change plus the AssertPermissionGated obligation — the exact shape mistral-vibe carried before commit 5e22e47. (2) ARCHITECTURE: the interrupt criterion stays unobservable even after that fix — an interrupted hermes turn persists no terminal row (finish_reason never 'stop', turn_exit_reason in-memory only, no turns table; sibling cell 2-20_user-esc-interrupt), so Watcher.turnIsDone stays false and the settle never fires. This cell is frozen rather than known_failing because a recording today would be a FALSE GREEN: the row's drivers inject with their own `tmux send-keys` and never call InputService, so the injected_turn/settle phases would pass while the capability under test does not exist, and the phase vocabulary (validate/expected.go: phase/expected_state/new_session/same_session_as) has no way to assert `controllable`. Unfreeze = (a) declare Control{SupportsInput:true, Interrupt:InterruptCtrlC} + agent.ControlPermission() in hermes/agent.go with a permission-gate test, (b) port an `interrupt` step into hermes/driver-interactive.sh sending C-c ONCE (Escape is not bound in Hermes; a second C-c within 2s force-exits), (c) for the interrupt criterion, the on_session_end hook tier (turn_finalizer.py:668-684 carries interrupted/completed per turn, bind-addr-aware per #1178). Then re-assess and add the session_birth -> injected_turn(working) -> settle(ready) phases. Observations: the store carries per-session input/output tokens on the sessions row, so tokens_nonzero holds; model and cost stay unpinned because the recorded model depends on the config.yaml under the run's HERMES_HOME.
